news.title: What working at the Oval taught me about the World Cup – and football’s soul
news.lede: This week UEFA and the FA are at war with FIFA over its plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors. It got me thinking about my week working hospitality at the Oval – where I expected snobbery but found something that made me wonder if any sport really belongs to its fans. In June, while England was gearing up to play Croatia in the World Cup, I worked in the hospitality section at The Oval as England’s cricketers faced New Zealand in a five-day Test. On day one, I arrived at the tube station, stunned by the number of people brimming with joy at the prospect of their ‘lavish’ week ahead.

news.title: Fifa to push ahead with 'open and democratic consultation' process over World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: Fifa will be pushing ahead with a consultation process about whether to sell off stakes in the World Cup and its other tournaments to private investors, despite widespread criticism of the proposal. The pushback since football's world governing body revealed its plan to sell a 20 per cent stake in a subsidiary company set up to run Fifa's competitions has been relentless. On Thursday, those protests reached fever pitch when Uefa, European football's governing body, announced that they will boycott the World Cup – and all Fifa's competitions – if the plan of president Gianni Infantino was not scrapped. “Some things are simply too important to sell,” Uefa said in a statement.

news.title: ‘Nobody is selling football’: FIFA hit back as Europe vows to boycott World Cup
news.lede: Updated July 31, 2026 - 4.49am. First published July 30, 2026 - 5.56pm. FIFA insist their plan to sell stakes in football’s biggest tournaments will “not come at the cost of the spirit or governance” of the sport, as the organisation prepares for the impact of European nations threats to boycott upcoming FIFA-run competitions. An urgent meeting held on Friday (AEST) by UEFA ended in all 55 of its member nations electing to boycott any further FIFA run tournaments, including the World Cup, as a result of Gianni Infantino’s private equity investment proposal.
